original_value: Compelling facial expression recognition (FER) processes have been utilized in very successful fields like computer vision, robotics, artificial intelligence, and dynamic texture recognition. However, the FER’s critical problem with traditional local binary pattern (LBP) is the loss of neighboring pixels related to different scales that can affect the texture of facial images. To overcome such limitations, this study describes a new extended LBP method to extract feature vectors from images, detecting each image from facial expressions. The proposed method is based on the bitwise AND operation of two rotational kernels applied on LBP(8,1) and LBP(8,2) and utilizes two accessible datasets. Firstly, the facial parts are detected and the essential components of a face are observed, such as eyes, nose, and lips. The portion of the face is then cropped to reduce the dimensions and an unsharp masking kernel is applied to sharpen the image. The filtered images then go through the feature extraction method and wait for the classification process. Four machine learning classifiers were used to verify the proposed method. This study shows that the proposed multi-scale featured local binary pattern (MSFLBP), together with Support Vector Machine (SVM), outperformed the recent LBP-based state-of-the-art approaches resulting in an accuracy of 99.12% for the Extended Cohn–Kanade (CK+) dataset and 89.08% for the Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces (KDEF) dataset.

result.paraphrase: Facial expression recognition (FER) has been widely applied in successful areas such as computer vision, robotics, artificial intelligence, and dynamic texture recognition. Yet a major drawback of conventional local binary pattern (LBP) in FER is that it can lose neighboring pixels across scales, which may degrade the texture information in facial images. To address this, the study introduces a novel extended LBP approach for extracting feature vectors from facial-expression images. The method uses a bitwise AND operation on two rotational kernels applied to LBP(8,1) and LBP(8,2), and it is evaluated on two publicly available datasets. First, facial regions are detected and key components such as the eyes, nose, and lips are identified. The face area is then cropped to reduce dimensions, and an unsharp masking kernel is applied to enhance sharpness. The filtered images are then passed to the feature extraction stage before classification. Four machine-learning classifiers were employed to validate the proposed method. Results show that the proposed multi-scale featured local binary pattern (MSFLBP), combined with Support Vector Machine (SVM), outperformed recent state-of-the-art LBP-based methods, achieving 99.12% accuracy on the Extended Cohn–Kanade (CK+) dataset and 89.08% on the Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces (KDEF) dataset.
